policy: Conservative manually maintained ledger, supported by independent reviews that may be performed by AI agents. Add a certification only after the full named environment has source review, compiled actual exports and permitted transitive axioms. Partial components, algorithms and source obstructions do not count. All unlisted named environments remain uncounted. This is not a percentage of the entire monograph. Record fields added on 2026-11-10 (project decision 2026-11-10, site redesign spec §5): `proof_origin` (source-proof: formalizes the book's argument; source-proof-repaired: the book's argument with gaps repaired, see the cited source issue; own-proof:source-cites: the book cites the literature and the Lean proof is this project's own; own-proof:source-omits: the book gives no proof and the Lean proof is this project's own), `display_note` (how the proved statement differs from the print), `correction_status` (proposed-by-project: the correction, restriction or repair is this project's proposal, not confirmed by the authors; none is author-confirmed). `status_override` may only downgrade a record's displayed status (currently only "incomplete" on Theorem 7.7). `entry_display_notes` holds display notes for statement entries that have no record here (superseded entries, reading aids and prose-claim entries).

entry_display_notes.Thm3_2_burnInNecessary_restricted: A restricted reading of the burn-in necessity claim: with N ≤ log(SA)/(8(1−γ)), every deterministic learner returning a deterministic policy has, on some instance, probability ≥ 1/4 of value gap $\Vert V^{\star} - V^{\hat{\pi}}\Vert_{\infty} > 1/(64(1-\gamma))$. "Strictly better than a random guess" is undefined in the book; this reading and the proof are this project's. Inherits S ≥ 2, A ≥ 2, SA ≥ 16, γ ∈ [2/3,1) from the corrected Theorem 3.7; accuracies between 1/(64(1−γ)) and 1/(1−γ) are not covered (C49).
entry_display_notes.Eq_P_Mi_Q_inaccurate_lower_generative: The two-point lower bound for every estimator, randomized included (a probability law on ℝ given the sample array): for γ ∈ [2/3,1), 0 < ε < 1/(32(1−γ)) and every N ≤ 0.003/((1−γ)³ε²), every estimator of Q(s₁,a) has P(|Q̂ − Q⋆| > ε) > 0.1 under one of two two-state, one-action MDPs. Deterministic estimators are the Dirac case; the strict inequality is the C4 step.
entry_display_notes.Remark4_3_corrected: The remark has no formula. Read like Remarks 4.1 and 4.2: with δ = ε(1−γ)/2 in Theorem 4.12's budget, E[max|Q_T − Q⋆|] ≤ 2ε, under the premises of the corrected Theorem 4.12 ($\mu_{\mathsf{min}} > 0$, and T ≥ 2 or SA ≥ 2). Without them this reading fails (T = 1 with SA = 1, or $\mu_{\mathsf{min}} = 0$; paper computation by this project, C34).
entry_display_notes.Eq_regret_asymptotic_ucbvi_corrected: Under the premises of the corrected Theorem 5.2 (zero-count completion, C8; c₁ = 4, c₂ = 16) and the burn-in S³AH³ ≤ K (constant 1): with probability ≥ 1 − δ, Regret(K) ≤ 40√(SAH³K)(1 + I), with I as in the corrected Theorem 5.2. The Õ is made explicit; the matching-lower-bound sentence is not separately formalized.
entry_display_notes.Remark5_5_corrected: For the UCBVI tables with the zero-count completion (C8), at every stage h and state s and for all bonus parameters: $V_{h}(s) = \max_{a}$ Q_h(s,a) = $Q_{h}(s, \pi_{h}(s))$ for the fixed greedy planner of the corrected Theorem 5.2. This is stronger than the printed h = 1. Only the table object is corrected; the identity does not depend on the bonus. The remark's proof-strategy sentences are not formalized.
entry_display_notes.Remark5_12_lowerBound: The lower bound, unrestricted: for 2 ≤ A ≤ T, a fixed family of A mean vectors in $[0,1]^{A}$ (Gaussian N(0,1) noise) on which every measurable randomized history-dependent learner has expected pseudo-regret ≥ (1/16)√(AT) on some member. The proof and the constant 1/16 are this project's; the remark only says that the argument adapts.
entry_display_notes.Remark5_12_restricted: Minimax optimality up to logarithmic factors: in addition, UCB's expected regret on every r ∈ $[0,1]^{A}$ is at most 128√log(T²/δ) times that lower bound. Restricted because it inherits Theorem 5.1's deterministic tie rule.
entry_display_notes.Remark5_13_corrected: $T_{6}^{\mathsf{ucb}} \le 2T_{6}^{\mathsf{low}} + 2T_{6}^{\mathsf{diff}}$ and $\sqrt{T_{6}^{\mathsf{ucb}}} \le \sqrt{2T_{6}^{\mathsf{low}}} + \sqrt{2T_{6}^{\mathsf{diff}}}$, deterministically. The inequalities are as printed; the quantities are those of the zero-count completion of the algorithm (C8), hence the suffix.
entry_display_notes.Eq_mdp_value_Q_restricted: One deterministic stationary policy maximizes the robust value at every state and the robust Q-function at every state-action pair, over all stationary randomized policies. Proved for the TV and support-aware χ² uncertainty sets and for every row-set family whose row infima are attained, σ > 0. Restricted because the book's general "distance-like" ρ is read as implying attainment; families without attained infima are not claimed (scope disclosure).
entry_display_notes.Eq_bellman_equ_infinite_all_restricted: The robust Bellman consistency and optimality equations: $Q^{\pi,\sigma}(s,a) = r(s,a) + \gamma \cdot \inf$ over $U^{\sigma}(P^{0}_{s,a})$ of $\langle P, V^{\pi,\sigma}\rangle$ for every stationary randomized π, and the same for Q⋆ and V⋆ (suprema attained), which every value-maximizing π⋆ attains. For TV, support-aware χ² and every row-set family with attained row infima, σ > 0; the general distance-like ρ is covered only when its row infima are attained (scope disclosure).
entry_display_notes.Eq_robust_bellman_fixedPoint_restricted: For TV, χ² and every row-set family with attained row infima, σ > 0: Q⋆ is the unique fixed point of the robust Bellman operator $T^{\sigma}$; $T^{\sigma}$ is a γ-contraction in sup norm; iterates from any Q₀ converge at rate $\gamma^{t}$, and DRVI from 0 is within $\gamma^{t}/(1-\gamma)$. Same attainment restriction as Eq. (7.4) (scope disclosure).
entry_display_notes.Remark7_1_restricted: Reading Õ((1−γ)²/N) as $c_{\mathsf{opt}}(1-\gamma)^{2}\log (SAN/((1-\gamma)\delta))/N$: for every $c_{\mathsf{opt}} \ge 0$ some C₂ makes Theorem 7.2's guarantee hold with probability ≥ 1 − δ, simultaneously for every deterministic planner output that meets the requirement. Randomized planner outputs are not covered. The book cites this without proof; the Lean proof is this project's.
entry_display_notes.Remark7_2_restricted: Reading O(log(SAN/((1−γ)δ))/N²) as $c_{\mathsf{opt}}\cdot \log (SAN/((1-\gamma)\delta))/N^{2}$: for every $c_{\mathsf{opt}} \ge 0$ some c₂ makes Theorem 7.4's guarantee hold under its premises, with probability ≥ 1 − δ, simultaneously for every deterministic planner output that meets the requirement. Randomized and history-dependent outputs are not covered. The book cites this without proof; the Lean proof is this project's.
entry_display_notes.Eq_sample_size_per_agent_fedQ_restricted: The per-agent sample size read off from the corrected Theorem 7.9, only in the range $c_{\eta}$ K(1−γ)⁴ε² ≤ log(SAK/δ): an explicit T with SA·T ≤ C·SA/(K(1−γ)⁵ε²)·(1 + log(SAK/(δε(1−γ)²)))³ samples per agent makes FedSynQ ε-accurate with probability ≥ 1 − δ. The read-off for all K is open, neither proved nor refuted (C41).
entry_display_notes.Eq_DPO_restricted: The DPO loss of $\pi_{r}$ equals the Bradley–Terry negative log-likelihood of r; every full-support policy is some $\pi_{r}$; $\pi_{r} = \pi_{r'}$ iff r − r' depends on the prompt only; the DPO minimizers over full-support policies are exactly the Gibbs policies of likelihood minimizers (existence not claimed). Restricted to full-support policies, full-support $\pi_{\mathsf{ref}}$ and finite prompt and response sets: over all policies the minimum can be attained only at boundary policies (scope disclosure).
entry_display_notes.Eq_policy_RBMLE_restricted: For sign ∈ {±1} and α, β > 0: the VPO objective at $\pi_{r}$ equals ℓ(r,D) − sign·α·J⋆(r;$\pi_{\mathsf{cal}}$); full-support VPO minimizers are the Gibbs policies of reward-space minimizers; $E[\log \pi - \log \pi_{\mathsf{cal}}] = -E_{\rho}$ $\mathsf{KL} (\pi_{\mathsf{cal}}\Vert \pi)$; swapping $\pi_{\mathsf{ref}}$ for $\pi_{\mathsf{cal}}$ shifts the objective by a constant. Same full-support restriction as the DPO display (scope disclosure).
entry_display_notes.Eq_online_RBMLE_restricted: For every minimizer r of ℓ(r,D) − αJ⋆(r;$\pi_{\mathsf{cal}}$), $\pi_{r}$ maximizes the KL-regularized value J(r,·) over all conditional policies and minimizes the online VPO objective over full-support policies. Existence and uniqueness of minimizers are not claimed (C44). Same full-support restriction as the DPO display (scope disclosure).
